summary: Displaay's Nuxt microsite for Azeret (captured from the Wayback Machine), a sans with Proportional, SemiMono and Mono sub-families on a 'mono' axis, inspired by OCR fonts and old operating systems: electric violet fields, lilac-tinted archival photos of computer consoles with WebGL transitions, dark 'anatomy' cards (construction lens, metric lines), typed-in-a-loop word showcases and floating 'Get Azeret' / 'Type tester' cards that follow the visitor down the page.

instances.look: 'Azeret' in pale lilac at huge size anchored bottom-right over a looping violet video with a glowing horizontal light band; tiny 'New Sans Serif' and '3 sub-families / 48 styles' top-left; two floating lilac cards top-right ('Get Azeret', 'Type tester')
instances.ux: Intro: a counter ('0') at the bottom-right, then the letters of 'azereT' animate in one by one before the name settles; the video loops behind
instances.learn: Push the wordmark into the bottom-right corner and let a slow light-band video carry the mood: the empty violet space reads as a screen

reconstruction.layout: Full-bleed 1440×900; name right-aligned at x≈380–1400, baseline at the bottom edge (~240px cap height, partly cropped); meta text 20px from top-left in two columns (x≈20, x≈375); cards 335px wide at x≈1085
reconstruction.typography: Name ~330px Azeret wght 500, colour #dcd8e3; meta ~20px Regular lilac
reconstruction.behaviour: Background <video loop muted playsinline>; on load a numeric counter, then per-letter spans of the name fade/slide in (customFade)
reconstruction.assets: Looping violet gradient video with a moving light band
reconstruction.html: Nuxt (data-v-*) section with <video> and the name split into per-letter spans

instances.look: A three-line statement on violet, 'New Sans-Serif with ③ Sub-Families & total ㊽ styles', with the numbers set small inside white discs within the line, followed by a wide lilac-tinted archival photo of a computer console with telephones and screens
instances.learn: Drop the key numbers into the sentence as small badges: the claim stays one readable line while the figures pop

reconstruction.layout: Statement from x≈20, ~3 lines × 125px; discs ~110px inline; photo full column (1420×780) below with 20px margin, rounded corners
reconstruction.typography: ~144px Azeret wght 500 pale lilac; disc numbers ~26px violet
reconstruction.assets: Archival photo of a control console, duotoned lilac

instances.look: 'Driven by study of OCR Fonts and Operating Systems.' in four big lines, a hairline rule, then a small 'Optical character recognition — Source: Wikipedia' label and two columns of quoted encyclopedia text with bold key phrases
instances.learn: Quote the encyclopedia definition of the inspiration, credited, instead of writing your own history

reconstruction.layout: Heading x≈20, 4 lines ~125px; rule at y≈660; label column x≈20; text columns at x≈735 and x≈1085, ~330px each
reconstruction.typography: Heading ~144px Azeret wght 500; label 13px; body ~14px with Bold highlights, lilac
reconstruction.content: Wikipedia text on optical character recognition

instances.look: A rounded near-black card labelled 'Construction in detail' with 'RCA 501' in solid violet; inside a thin violet circle the letters turn into outlines with their on-curve points
instances.ux: The circle is a lens drawn on a canvas that reveals the outline and points of whatever it covers (likely follows the pointer)
instances.learn: Use a moving lens to switch the letters from fill to outline-with-points: construction shown only where the visitor looks

reconstruction.layout: Card 1400×1000px with 20px violet margin and ~10px radius; label top-left (x≈60,y≈40); word centred ~1000px wide; lens ~320px diameter
reconstruction.typography: Word ~200px Azeret wght 500 violet #8b1be6; label 15px lilac
reconstruction.behaviour: Canvas (1400×1001) renders filled glyphs outside the lens and outline + points inside it; lens position updates with the cursor
reconstruction.assets: Glyph outline data for the canvas

instances.look: Split row: a lilac card 'Showcase of selected alternates' where words such as 'QWERTY_' and 'Programma_' are typed and erased in violet with a blinking underscore caret; beside it a lilac-tinted archival photo of computer hardware that morphs into the next photo
instances.ux: Autoplay: vue-typer types a word, pauses, erases, types the next; the photo column cross-dissolves through 6 images with a WebGL distortion
instances.learn: Type the alternates in a loop with a terminal caret: the feature is shown in the medium that inspired it

reconstruction.behaviour: vue-typer (char spans .typed/.erased, smooth caret); WebGL canvas 800×600 transitions between images

instances.look: On violet, three short stats appear one per screen in the centre, '48 styles', '3 sub-families', '1 for free', each fading and slanting into the next (the outgoing line turns faint and italic)
instances.ux: Pinned while scrolling; each stat transitions to the next; a black circular 'Test them all!' button sits under each (mobile)
instances.learn: Animate between stats with the font's own italic: the transition itself shows a style

instances.look: Three ruled rows on violet: 'Proportional Version', 'SemiMono Version', 'Mono Version', each heading and its two sample paragraphs (a large lead and a small body about the history of OCR) set in that sub-family

instances.learn: Set the same text in each sub-family side by side so the mono axis is felt in real paragraphs, then put the price at the end of each row
